# venice-bridge

> venice-bridge is a free, open-source local bridge for macOS that lets OpenCode and other OpenAI-compatible coding agents use a venice.ai web subscription, with working tool calls.

Version 0.1.0 · MIT · Repository: https://github.com/nsozturk/venice-bridge · Docs: https://nsozturk.github.io/venice-bridge/

## Overview

venice-bridge is one Python file (`venice_bridge.py`, about 1,900 lines) plus `tolerant_parser.py`. It runs an HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:18891` that speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, and forwards each request to the backend of the venice.ai web app, authenticated with your own browser login. It does not use the paid Venice API and needs no API key.

### Disclaimer

- Unofficial. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Venice.ai.
- It talks to undocumented web endpoints that can change or break at any time.
- It automates your own logged-in web session; that may be against Venice's terms of service. You use it at your own risk, with your own account.
- Do not share cookies or accounts. The cookie is a live credential for your Venice account: never commit it, never share it.

## Requirements

- macOS. The bridge streams through the system `curl`, which passes Cloudflare. Linux and Windows are untested.
- Python 3.10+ and `curl_cffi` (`pip install curl_cffi`).
- A venice.ai web account, logged in in your browser. Everything was tested on a paid plan (Pro). The agent route needs a paid plan (a free account gets `403 creator_access_required`); a free account has a very small chat quota.
- OpenCode, or any client that speaks OpenAI Chat Completions.
- Not supported: Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) and OpenAI Responses (`/v1/responses`), so Claude Code and Codex CLI do not work with it directly.

## Quick start

1. Get the code and the dependency:

```
git clone https://github.com/nsozturk/venice-bridge.git
cd venice-bridge
pip install curl_cffi
```

2. Save your login cookie (the only setup step). The bridge needs the value of the `__client` cookie of `clerk.venice.ai` (a long-lived Clerk cookie). From it the bridge mints a session JWT of about 60 seconds and a client attestation for every request window. Log in on venice.ai in Chrome, open DevTools → Application → Cookies → `https://clerk.venice.ai`, copy the Value of `__client`, then:

```
mkdir -p ~/.config/venice-bridge && pbpaste > ~/.config/venice-bridge/client-cookie.txt && chmod 600 ~/.config/venice-bridge/client-cookie.txt
```

The file may hold the bare value or a pasted `__client=...;` string. Override its path with `VENICE_BRIDGE_COOKIE_FILE`. Clerk rotates the cookie while it is used; the bridge saves the rotated value to `~/.config/venice-bridge/rotated-client.json` (mode 0600, override with `VENICE_BRIDGE_CLIENT_FILE`).

Optional second source: a local session daemon. Set `VENICE_BRIDGE_SESSION_DIR` to a folder containing a `client.py` that exposes `get_session(domain)` returning `{"timestamp": <ms>, "tokens": {"clerk_client": "<value>"}}`. The cookie file wins when both are present.

3. Run the bridge: `python3 venice_bridge.py` (options `--host`, `--port`; default 127.0.0.1:18891). It prints `[+] Venice AI Bridge listening on http://127.0.0.1:18891/v1`. Logs go to stderr.

4. Check it: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18891/health` answers `{"ok": true, "venice_session": "active", "chat_quota": {...}}`. Offline self-check without network: `python3 test_venice_bridge.py` prints `cookie file ok`, `session ok`, `ok`, `end to end ok`.

5. Add the provider to OpenCode: copy the provider block from `examples/opencode.json` into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (or a project `opencode.json`). Shortened to one model:

```
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "venice-bridge": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Venice Web (local bridge)",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18891/v1",
        "apiKey": "local"
      },
      "models": {
        "deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored": {
          "name": "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Uncensored (Venice Web)",
          "modalities": { "input": ["text"], "output": ["text"] },
          "limit": { "context": 524288, "output": 131072 }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Models in the example config: deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored, deepseek-v4-1-flash, z-ai-glm-5-3-flash, kimi-k2-5, default, qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct-turbo, qwen3-6-27b, zai-org-glm-5.2, venice-uncensored-1-2. `GET /v1/models` lists whatever the account's web catalogue offers without credits.

6. First run: `opencode -m venice-bridge/deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored`

## Autostart (launchd)

`examples/com.example.venice-bridge.plist` is a launchd template: `RunAtLoad`, `KeepAlive`, `ThrottleInterval` 60, stdout and stderr to `venice_bridge.log` in the repository folder. Replace every `/PATH/TO` with real absolute paths, copy it to `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, then:

```
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.venice-bridge.plist
```

## How it works

Flow: client (OpenAI Chat Completions) → venice-bridge on 127.0.0.1:18891 → `clerk.venice.ai` (the `__client` cookie gives a session and a ~60 s JWT) and `outerface.venice.ai` (client attestation, then the chat request on the route chosen by `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE`: by default the chat route `/api/inference/chat`, JSON lines; as fallback the agent route `/api/inference/chat/agents/ad-hoc`, Responses-style SSE). The reply goes through the call readers and tool routing and comes back as OpenAI chunks or `tool_calls`. A 401 from Venice is retried once with a fresh JWT and attestation.

### Routes

`VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE` = `auto` (default) | `chat` | `agent`.

- `chat`: `POST outerface.venice.ai/api/inference/chat`, the web app's plain chat route (JSON lines, one object per line with a `kind`). Venice runs no agent loop there and gives the model no tools of its own, so nothing collides with the client's tools and no call is swallowed. The client's system prompt is folded into the first user message (`[SESSION INSTRUCTIONS] … [END OF SESSION INSTRUCTIONS]`, then `[USER REQUEST]`), because that route's `413 userPromptTooLong` limit (about 150,000 characters) applies to the `systemPrompt` field only; 460,000 characters inside a user message were accepted (measured). The route sends no closing event, so a clean end of the HTTP response (curl exit code 0) is the completion signal.
- `agent`: `POST outerface.venice.ai/api/inference/chat/agents/ad-hoc`, the agent route (Responses-style SSE). Needs a paid plan (a free account gets `403 creator_access_required`). Venice runs its own agent loop there: the model gets Venice's server tools as native tools; a native call to a client tool is swallowed (the stream shows only the tool name, never the arguments, so it cannot be forwarded), and Venice's own `get_attachment` / `view_media` run with made-up ids. Turns can end in "my tools are not available / Tool not found".
- `auto`: use `chat`; if Venice answers `400 modelNotFound` for a model (measured for `kimi-k2-5`), remember that model (until the bridge restarts) and use `agent` for it.

The log line `timing open: … route=chat|agent` shows which route a request used. Everything was measured on a paid (Pro) account.

### Tool emulation and the tiered tool list

Venice's web routes do not give the model the client's declared tools (measured on the agent route `/agents/ad-hoc` and on `/agents/venice`: a declared `bash` client tool is invisible to the model; the chat route offers the model no tools). So tools are emulated in text. The tool list goes into the system prompt: built-in tools and tools already used in the conversation get a compact full JSON schema (tier A), the rest are one-liners (tier B), inside a 78,000-character budget. Over budget, tier B degrades from the end to shorter descriptions, then names only; tier A is never cut. A real OpenCode request measured 411 tools and about 441,000 characters of system prompt. The model replies `{"tool_calls":[{"name":"...","arguments":{...}}]}`; a format reminder with one example is appended as the last user message.

### Tolerant parser

`tolerant_parser.py` (a port of the opencode-venice-web parser, MIT) reads calls that are bare, fenced, after prose, in several envelopes, or structurally broken (8 of 8 real malformed replies in the fixtures). ### Call readers

- Native call reader: some models write tool calls in their own markup, with arguments, as text. On the chat route DeepSeek V4.1 Flash writes `<｜DSML｜ invoke name="shell"><｜DSML｜ parameter name="command" string="true">ls</｜DSML｜ parameter></｜DSML｜ invoke>`. The bridge reads that form and plain `<invoke name=…><parameter name=…>`, several calls per reply, takes `string="false"` parameters as JSON, and never shows the markup as text.
- Tagged call reader: `<tool_calls>{"name":…,"arguments":…}</tool_calls>`, including file content with unescaped quotes.

### Tool routing

A call to a tool the client did not declare is routed to the client's tool for the same job. A call to an unknown name with no counterpart is passed to the client when the reply is only that call (under 200 characters of other text), so the client can tell the model; otherwise it is dropped and logged.

| The model calls | Routed to |
|---|---|
| `cat`, `read_file`, `view` | `read` |
| `shell`, `execute`, `run_command` | `bash` (or `shell` on clients that name it so) |
| `str_replace`, `edit_file` | `edit` |
| `create_file`, `write_file` | `write` |
| `search`, `rg` | `grep` |
| `find_files` | `glob` |
| `web_search` | `websearch` |
| `web_scrape`, `fetch` | `webfetch` |
| `ls`, `list_dir` | `list`, or a shell `ls` |
| Venice's `get_attachment`, `view_media` | `read`, only when the id is a file path |

The tool block in the prompt also tells the model that Venice's own tools and built-in function calling do not reach this computer, and which client tool does which job (read a file, run a command, search the web, fetch a web page).

### Argument fitting

Arguments the model named differently are renamed: `path` / `file_path` / `filename` → `filePath`, `cmd` / `script` → `command`, `old_str` → `oldString`, `new_str` → `newString`, `contents` / `text` → `content`, `query` / `regex` → `pattern`, `link` → `url`. This happens only when the tool expects that name, did not get it, and does not know the other name.

### Completion check

A reply counts only after its completion signal: `response.completed` on the agent route; on the chat route, which sends no closing event, a clean end of the HTTP response (curl exit code 0). A cut stream never becomes a half-written file.

### Server-loop cut (agent route only)

On the agent route Venice sometimes takes a model's native tool call for one of its own server tools, or runs one of its own tools, and answers the model "Tool not found" in a loop. The bridge tolerates 3 such steps, then cuts the response and retries with a reminder that names the tools. Cutting at the first step in which Venice runs its own tool was tried and removed: it made DeepSeek V4.1 Flash fail 7 of 8 turns, because the model usually recovers inside the same response.

### In-bridge retries

In tools mode the bridge retries by itself, budget 2 (`VENICE_BRIDGE_FORMAT_RETRIES`), for: server loop, unreadable call, empty reply, broken stream (resent once, unchanged). Each retry adds a targeted reminder and is a full upstream request; a retry never replaces a better reply. A reply that was already streamed live (see the stream gate) is neither retried nor judged.

### Judge

When a reply ends the turn right after a tool result without calling a tool, a small judge model (`qwen3-5-35b-a3b`) checks it for an early stop, an ignored failure or a missing result, and can trigger one more attempt (`VENICE_BRIDGE_JUDGE_RETRIES`, default 1). It only sees the latest user request, the last two tool results and the reply, as tails. Any judge failure keeps the reply. Disable it with `VENICE_BRIDGE_JUDGE=0`.

### Stream gate

With tools, a prose reply longer than 200 characters is streamed while it is written; anything that may still become a tool call is held back. Failures before the status line are returned as HTTP 502, because OpenCode retries a 502 but not an error inside a started stream (measured). Without tools, text and reasoning stream as they arrive. A stream that fails after it started ends with a `data: {"error": {...}}` line and no `data: [DONE]`, never with a normal ending.

### Error mapping

| Upstream situation | Client sees | Error type |
|---|---|---|
| Chat quota used up (Venice 429, 0 remaining) | 403 | `venice_quota_exhausted` (body code 429), message with the reset time |
| Passing rate limit (Venice 429, quota left) | 429 | `venice_rate_limited` |
| Request too large (Venice 413) | 400 | `invalid_request_error`, code `context_length_exceeded` |
| Cloudflare challenge | 502 | `venice_upstream_error` (body code 403), with a clear message |
| Model not on the chat route (Venice 400 `modelNotFound`) | with `auto`: sent to the agent route; with `chat`: 502 | `venice_upstream_error` (body code 400), "Venice answered HTTP 400: …" |
| Plan or credits do not cover the model (Venice 402) | 402 | `venice_upstream_error` |
| Auth rejected (Venice 401 after one retry, or 403) | 401 / 403 | `venice_upstream_error` |
| Other upstream failure, empty or cut reply | 502 | `venice_upstream_error` or `bridge_error` |

The quota is answered as 403 on purpose: OpenCode retries a 429 silently. While the quota is known to be used up, the bridge answers at once without calling Venice; `POST /reload` clears that lock.

## Configuration

Command-line options: `--host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `--port` (default `18891`).

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE` | `auto` | Venice web route: `auto` (chat route; agent route for a model the chat route does not know), `chat` (chat route only), `agent` (agent route only; needs a paid plan) |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_COOKIE_FILE` | `~/.config/venice-bridge/client-cookie.txt` | Text file with the `__client` cookie value |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_SESSION_DIR` | unset | Folder with a local session daemon's `client.py` exposing `get_session(domain)` |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_CLIENT_FILE` | `~/.config/venice-bridge/rotated-client.json` | Where the rotated Clerk cookie is saved (mode 0600) |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_FORMAT_RETRIES` | `2` | In-bridge retries for server loop, unreadable call, empty reply, broken stream |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_JUDGE` | on | `0` turns the judge off |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_JUDGE_MODEL` | `qwen3-5-35b-a3b` | Model used as the judge |
| `VENICE_BRIDGE_JUDGE_RETRIES` | `1` | Extra attempts the judge may trigger |

## API reference

Base URL `http://127.0.0.1:18891`. Errors use the OpenAI shape `{"error": {"message", "type"}}`; upstream errors also carry `code`, while 404 and invalid-JSON errors carry only `message`. `/health` uses its own shape. Unknown paths answer 404.

### POST /v1/chat/completions

OpenAI Chat Completions, streaming (`"stream": true`, server-sent events ending with `data: [DONE]`) and non-streaming. Declared `tools` come back as `tool_calls` with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`; reasoning text arrives as `reasoning_content` deltas. If `model` is missing, `qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct-turbo` is used.

```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18891/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with PONG"}]}'
```

Status codes: 200 (completion or SSE stream); 400 (invalid JSON, or `context_length_exceeded`); 401/403 (Venice rejected the login, or the agent route on a free account with `creator_access_required`; type `venice_upstream_error`); 402 (plan or credits do not cover the model); 403 (quota used up; type `venice_quota_exhausted`); 429 (passing rate limit; type `venice_rate_limited`); 502 (upstream failure, Cloudflare challenge, empty or cut reply).

### GET /v1/models

Lists the models of the account's web catalogue that do not use credits (`owned_by: "venice-web"`). 502 (`bridge_error`) when the catalogue cannot be read.

```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18891/v1/models
```

### GET /health

200 `{"ok": true, "venice_session": "active", "chat_quota": {"reset_at", "remaining", "resets_in_min"}}` when a session JWT can be minted; `chat_quota` is `null` when the quota cannot be read. 503 `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` when the login does not work.

```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18891/health
```

### POST /reload

Drops the cached auth (Clerk cookie, session, JWT, attestation) and the quota lock. 200 `{"ok": true}`.

```
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18891/reload
```

## Measured performance

Measured in November 2026 on one machine with one account. These are observations, not guarantees.

- Bridge overhead per request: about 21 ms with a 441k-character prompt and 401 tools (local fake upstream).
- A short model step through the bridge: 1.5–3 s; a warm OpenCode session: 2.8–4.5 s per message.
- On the agent route, swallowed calls cost roughly 20–50 % of bridge time on models that prefer native tool calls; on the chat route none were seen.

Small-project benchmark (the coding client builds a Python todo CLI with tests and a README from one prompt), wall time including the client's own startup:

| Model id | Route used | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| deepseek-v4-1-flash | chat | working project, 3 of 3 runs, 0 retries, 0 swallowed calls | 34–51 s |
| deepseek-v4-1-flash (before, agent route) | agent | 2 of 4 runs produced a project | 63–203 s |
| deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored | chat | working project, 3 of 3 runs | 16 s, 56 s, and one 460 s run where the model itself took 86 steps to debug a test |
| z-ai-glm-5-3-flash | chat | working project | 84 s |
| qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct-turbo | chat | working project | 86 s |
| kimi-k2-5 | agent (not on the chat route) | commands work, its own tests left failing | 146 s |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Connection refused on port 18891 | The bridge is not running | Start `python3 venice_bridge.py`, or check `venice_bridge.log` when launchd runs it |
| `/health` answers 503 | No cookie, or Clerk no longer accepts it | Copy a fresh `__client` value into the cookie file, then `POST /reload` |
| 403 `creator_access_required` (type `venice_upstream_error`) | The request went to the agent route on a free Venice account | The agent route needs a paid Venice web plan (Pro); with `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE=agent`, try `auto` |
| 403 type `venice_quota_exhausted` | Web chat quota used up | Wait for the reset time in the message; `/health` shows `resets_in_min` |
| 429 type `venice_rate_limited` | Venice is rate limiting briefly; quota is left | Retry after a short wait |
| 502 "Cloudflare challenged the request" | Cloudflare wants a browser check | Open venice.ai in your browser, refresh the cookie file (or sync your session daemon), try again |
| 400 `context_length_exceeded` | The request is larger than Venice accepts | Start a new session or compact the conversation; declare fewer tools |
| 402 | Plan or credits do not cover the model | Pick a model from `GET /v1/models` |
| The model stops early or a tool call fails now and then | Tool calling is emulated; open models sometimes need a retry | Ask again or switch models (see the benchmark) |
| Short replies appear all at once in tools mode | The stream gate holds replies under 200 characters until complete | Expected behaviour |
| The model says its tools are unavailable, or "Tool not found" (for example "the tool layer is down — shell, execute and read all return Tool not found") | The request went through the agent route (check `route=` in the log) | Use `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE=auto` or `chat`, or pick a model that exists on the chat route. In an existing conversation the model may keep believing its tools are broken: tell it they work now, or start a new session |
| 502 "Venice answered HTTP 400: … modelNotFound" with `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE=chat` | That model exists only on the agent route | Use `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE=auto` |

## FAQ

### Does it need a Venice API key?

No. venice-bridge does not use the paid Venice API. It talks to the backend of the venice.ai web app with your own browser login (the `__client` cookie of `clerk.venice.ai`). The `apiKey` value in the OpenCode config is a placeholder that the bridge does not check.

### Does it work on a free Venice account?

It was not tested on one. Everything was measured on a paid Venice web plan (Pro). The agent route needs a paid plan; on a free account it answers 403 creator_access_required. A free account also has a very small chat quota (about 5 messages per ~4 hours when it was observed).

### Does it work with Claude Code or Codex?

Not directly. The bridge speaks OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`) only. It does not implement the Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) or the OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`), which Claude Code and Codex CLI use.

### Does it work on Linux or Windows?

Untested. The bridge streams through the system `curl` of macOS, which passes Cloudflare. Linux and Windows have not been tried.

### Is this allowed by Venice?

venice-bridge is unofficial and not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Venice.ai. It automates your own logged-in web session through undocumented endpoints, which may be against Venice's terms of service. Use it at your own risk, with your own account only, and never share cookies or accounts.

### Where do my chats go?

From your client to the bridge on `127.0.0.1`, then to the venice.ai web backend under your own account (`clerk.venice.ai` for login, `outerface.venice.ai` for inference), as with the web app. When the judge is on, a short excerpt of the turn is sent to Venice as a second request. The bridge keeps no conversation history: each request body sits in a private temporary folder (mode 0700) only while its upstream call runs and is deleted afterwards. Its log records sizes, timings and outcomes and can include short excerpts of unreadable replies or swallowed tool calls.

### Is it an alternative to opencode-venice-web?

Yes, it is an independent Python implementation of the same idea. opencode-venice-web (Node) is the most mature Venice web proxy and sends the full schema of every tool; venice-bridge is one Python file that sends a tiered tool list within a fixed budget. Its tolerant tool-call parser is a port of the opencode-venice-web parser (MIT).

## Limits

- macOS only so far; no Anthropic Messages or OpenAI Responses API; no images.
- With tools, short replies are sent only when complete; long prose is streamed while it is written.
- Native tool calling does not exist on Venice's web routes for client tools (measured: a declared client tool is invisible to the model); everything is text emulation plus the call readers above.
- Tool calling is emulated; open models sometimes need a retry.

## Alternatives

- CanArslanDev/opencode-venice-web (https://github.com/CanArslanDev/opencode-venice-web): Node; the most mature Venice web proxy; sends full schemas for every tool.
- aintlikeu/unofficial-venice-proxy and zalo-alex/venice-opencode: other Venice web proxies.
- The official Venice API with an API key (metered credits), and OpenCode's built-in `venice` provider.

## AI agent integration

- `AGENTS.md` (https://github.com/nsozturk/venice-bridge/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the contract for agents that work on or with this repository.
- `GLOBAL_AGENT_RULE.md` (https://github.com/nsozturk/venice-bridge/blob/main/GLOBAL_AGENT_RULE.md): a standalone snippet to paste into your own agent's instructions.
